note: Places the Gospels record Our Lord going, and the moments of His life in a traditional harmony of the four Gospels. References: New American Bible, Revised Edition. Built by scripts/jesus/build.py.

places.m: Basilica of the Annunciation, Nazareth
places.s: The town of the Holy Family in Lower Galilee. The Basilica of the Annunciation stands over the grotto venerated as the home of the Virgin Mary, and the Church of Saint Joseph nearby recalls the carpenter's workshop.

places.m: Church of the Visitation, Ein Karem
places.s: Saint Luke names only "a town of Judah" in the hill country (Luke 1:39). Since the early centuries tradition has honoured Ein Karem, west of Jerusalem, as the home of Zechariah and Elizabeth.

places.m: Church of the Nativity, Bethlehem
places.s: The town of David. Saint Justin Martyr already wrote in the second century of the cave where Christ was born; the Grotto of the Nativity lies beneath the basilica built by Saint Helena.

places.m: Beit Sahour, east of Bethlehem
places.s: Luke says the shepherds were "in that region" (Luke 2:8). The Franciscan Shepherds' Field chapel in Beit Sahour keeps the memory of the angels' song.

places.m: Temple Mount, Old City of Jerusalem
places.s: The platform of Herod's Temple, the house of the Father where Our Lord was presented, was found at twelve, and taught at the great feasts.

places.m: Church of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, Old Cairo
places.s: Saint Matthew names only Egypt. Coptic tradition traces the Holy Family's route through many towns along the Nile; the crypt of Saints Sergius and Bacchus in Old Cairo is honoured as one of their resting places.

places.m: Al-Maghtas and Qasr al-Yahud, near Jericho
places.s: Saint John places the baptism at "Bethany across the Jordan" (John 1:28). The traditional site lies on both banks of the river east of Jericho: Al-Maghtas in Jordan and Qasr al-Yahud on the west bank.

places.m: Mount of Temptation, above Jericho
places.s: The Gospels say only "the desert". Tradition honours the Mount of Temptation above Jericho, where a Greek Orthodox monastery clings to the cliff.

places.m: Kafr Kanna, near Nazareth
places.s: Pilgrims have long honoured Kafr Kanna, where the Franciscan Wedding Church stands. Some scholars prefer Khirbet Qana, a ruin about 13 km to the north.

places.m: Capernaum, on the Sea of Galilee
places.s: "His own town" (Matthew 9:1), the center of His Galilean ministry. Pilgrims see the white synagogue built over an earlier one, and the house of Saint Peter beneath a modern church.

places.m: Sea of Galilee (Lake of Gennesaret, Sea of Tiberias)
places.s: The lake at the heart of Our Lord's ministry, where the apostles fished and where He calmed the wind and waves.

places.m: Bir Ya'qub, Nablus (ancient Sychar)
places.s: One of the most securely identified places in the Gospels: the well Jacob dug, now inside a Greek Orthodox church at the foot of Mount Gerizim.

places.m: Church of the Beatitudes, above Tabgha
places.s: Matthew says only that He "went up the mountain" (Matthew 5:1). The hill above Tabgha has been honoured since the fourth century; today's church has eight sides, for the eight Beatitudes.

places.m: Nein, south of Mount Tabor
places.s: A small village on the slope of the Hill of Moreh. A Franciscan chapel marks where Our Lord met the funeral procession.

places.m: Church of Saint Anne, Old City of Jerusalem
places.s: Archaeologists have uncovered the pool with five porticoes beside the Church of Saint Anne, honoured as the birthplace of the Virgin Mary.

places.m: Kursi, on the eastern shore of the Sea of Galilee
places.s: Mark and Luke say "the territory of the Gerasenes", Matthew "of the Gadarenes". A Byzantine monastery at Kursi, on the eastern shore, marks the traditional place.

places.m: Church of the Multiplication, Tabgha
places.s: Luke sets the feeding near Bethsaida (Luke 9:10). Since the fourth century pilgrims have honoured it at Tabgha, where the famous mosaic of the loaves and fishes lies before the altar.

places.m: Tyre, Lebanon
places.s: The Phoenician coast north of Galilee, the one journey of Our Lord outside the land of Israel during His ministry.

places.m: Hippos (Sussita), above the eastern shore
places.s: Mark says He went "into the district of the Decapolis" (Mark 7:31), a league of Greek cities east of the lake. The exact place of these signs is not named; Hippos, the Decapolis city nearest the lake, stands for the region here.

places.m: Magdala, on the western shore
places.s: Matthew writes Magadan, Mark Dalmanutha (Mark 8:10). Many identify the place with Magdala, the home town of Saint Mary Magdalene, where a first-century synagogue has been found.

places.m: Bethsaida, north of the Sea of Galilee
places.s: The home of Peter, Andrew and Philip (John 1:44). Archaeologists dispute between et-Tell and el-Araj, near the Jordan's entry into the lake.

places.m: Banias, at the foot of Mount Hermon
places.s: A pagan city at the springs of the Jordan, under a great rock face. Here, before shrines to the god Pan, Peter confessed Jesus as the Christ.

places.m: Basilica of the Transfiguration, Mount Tabor
places.s: The Gospels say "a high mountain" (Mark 9:2). Since Origen and Saint Cyril of Jerusalem, tradition has named Tabor; the Franciscan basilica crowns its summit.

places.m: Korazim, above Capernaum
places.s: A town of black basalt in the hills above Capernaum, one of the places where "most of His mighty deeds had been done" (Matthew 11:20-21).

places.m: Al-Eizariya, on the Mount of Olives
places.s: The village of Martha, Mary and Lazarus on the far slope of the Mount of Olives. The tomb of Lazarus and a Franciscan church are visited there.

places.m: City of David, Jerusalem
places.s: The pool at the south end of the City of David, fed by Hezekiah's tunnel. Its first-century steps were uncovered in 2004.

places.m: Church of the Pater Noster (Eleona), Mount of Olives
places.s: Saint Helena built the Eleona church over a cave where tradition says Our Lord taught His disciples. The Our Father is written on its walls in more than 140 languages.

places.m: Taybeh, north-east of Jerusalem
places.s: John says only that it was a town near the desert (John 11:54). Tradition places it at Taybeh, today a Christian village.

places.m: Jericho
places.s: The oasis city on the road up to Jerusalem. A sycamore tree in the town recalls Zacchaeus.

places.m: Franciscan church of Bethphage, Mount of Olives
places.s: The village where the disciples found the colt. The Palm Sunday procession of the Church in Jerusalem still begins here each year.

places.m: Church of Dominus Flevit, Mount of Olives
places.s: A small church shaped like a teardrop, looking across the Kidron to the city, recalls where "the Lord wept".

places.m: The Cenacle, Mount Zion
places.s: The early Church honoured Mount Zion as the place of the Last Supper and of Pentecost. The present Gothic room dates from the Crusades and the Franciscans.

places.m: Church of All Nations, at the foot of the Mount of Olives
places.s: The garden of ancient olive trees, with the Church of All Nations built over the rock where Our Lord prayed in agony.

places.m: Saint Peter in Gallicantu, Mount Zion
places.s: The Church of Saint Peter in Gallicantu ("at the cock's crow") keeps the memory of Peter's denial and of the night Our Lord spent in prison. Others place the high priest's house nearer the Cenacle.
places.w: Church of Saint Peter in Gallicantu

places.m: Church of the Flagellation and Ecce Homo arch, Via Dolorosa
places.s: The Way of the Cross begins at the Antonia fortress, where the Franciscans keep the Chapels of the Flagellation and Condemnation. Many scholars place Pilate instead at Herod's palace near the Jaffa Gate.

places.m: The Way of the Cross, Old City of Jerusalem
places.s: Since the Middle Ages pilgrims have prayed the Stations of the Cross along this street from the Antonia fortress to Calvary; the Franciscans lead the procession every Friday. The exact route Our Lord walked depends on where Pilate judged Him.

places.m: Church of the Holy Sepulchre, Jerusalem
places.s: Christians have honoured this place since the first generations; Saint Helena and Constantine built the basilica over the rock of Golgotha and the empty tomb, and the Franciscans serve there today.

places.m: Emmaus Nicopolis, near Latrun
places.s: Luke gives the distance as about seven miles from Jerusalem (Luke 24:13). Three sites are honoured: Emmaus Nicopolis, shown here; El-Qubeibeh, kept by the Franciscans; and Abu Ghosh.

places.n: Shore of the Sea of Tiberias
places.m: Church of the Primacy of Saint Peter, Tabgha
places.s: A small basalt church on the water's edge is built around the rock called Mensa Christi, the table of Christ, where tradition says He served breakfast to the apostles.
places.w: Church of the Primacy of Saint Peter

places.m: Chapel of the Ascension, Mount of Olives
places.s: Luke says He led them "as far as Bethany" (Luke 24:50), and Acts that they returned from the Mount of Olives (Acts 1:12). A small chapel at the summit keeps a rock honoured as bearing His last footprint.

events.s: The angel Gabriel greets the Virgin Mary, full of grace. At her "May it be done to me according to your word", the Word becomes flesh in her womb.
Mary carries Our Lord to her kinswoman Elizabeth. John leaps for joy in the womb, Elizabeth calls her "the mother of my Lord", and Mary sings the Magnificat.
Our Lord is born of the Virgin Mary in the city of David, wrapped in swaddling clothes and laid in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn.
An angel announces "a savior who is Messiah and Lord", and the heavenly host sings "Glory to God in the highest". The shepherds hurry to find the Child.
Wise men from the East follow His star, find the Child with Mary His mother, and offer gold, frankincense and myrrh.
Mary and Joseph present the Child to the Lord. Simeon takes Him in his arms, calls Him "a light for revelation to the Gentiles", and tells Mary a sword will pierce her heart.
Warned in a dream, Saint Joseph rises by night and takes the Child and His mother into Egypt, beyond the reach of Herod, fulfilling "Out of Egypt I called my son" (Hosea 11:1).
After Herod's death the Holy Family settles in Nazareth, and "the child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom; and the favor of God was upon him".
At twelve He stays behind in Jerusalem after Passover. On the third day Mary and Joseph find Him among the teachers: "Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?"
For some thirty years He lives at Nazareth, obedient to Mary and Joseph, working as a carpenter and advancing in wisdom and age and favor before God and man.
John baptizes Him in the Jordan. The heavens open, the Holy Spirit descends like a dove, and the Father's voice says: "This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased."
Led by the Spirit into the desert, He fasts forty days and forty nights and overcomes the temptations of the devil with the word of God.
John points Him out: "Behold, the Lamb of God." Andrew brings his brother Simon, whom Jesus names Cephas, Peter; Philip and Nathanael follow.
At His mother's word, "Do whatever he tells you", He changes water into wine, the first of His signs, and His disciples begin to believe in Him.

events.t: The first Passover: zeal for His Father's house
events.s: He drives the money changers from the Temple, and by night teaches Nicodemus that one must be born of water and Spirit. "God so loved the world that he gave his only Son."
Weary at noon, He asks a Samaritan woman for a drink and offers her living water, "a spring of water welling up to eternal life". Many in her town come to believe.
A royal official from Capernaum begs Him to come. "You may go; your son will live." The boy is healed at that very hour.

In the synagogue He reads Isaiah, "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me", and says, "Today this scripture passage is fulfilled." His own townspeople drive Him toward the brow of the hill, but He passes through their midst.
events.u: The Franciscans honour the Mount of the Precipice south of the town as the hill of Luke 4:29.

events.t: The Kingdom of God is at hand
events.s: Leaving Nazareth, He makes His home in Capernaum by the sea and begins to preach: "This is the time of fulfillment. The kingdom of God is at hand. Repent, and believe in the gospel."
By the shore He calls Simon and Andrew, James and John: "Come after me, and I will make you fishers of men." After the miraculous catch they leave everything and follow Him.
He teaches with authority in the synagogue, frees a man from an unclean spirit, raises Peter's mother-in-law from her fever, and at sunset the whole town gathers at the door.

events.t: The paralytic and the call of Matthew
events.s: Friends lower a paralyzed man through the roof; Jesus forgives his sins and bids him walk. Then He calls Levi, Matthew, from his customs post: "Follow me."
He teaches the Beatitudes, "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven", the new law of love, and the Our Father.
A Roman centurion says, "Lord, I am not worthy to have you enter under my roof; only say the word." The Church echoes his words before Holy Communion at every Mass.
Moved with pity for a widow burying her only son, He touches the bier: "Young man, I tell you, arise!" and gives him back to his mother.
At a feast in Jerusalem He heals a man ill for thirty-eight years: "Rise, take up your mat, and walk."
A violent squall swamps the boat while He sleeps. He rebukes the wind, "Quiet! Be still!", and there is great calm. "Who then is this whom even wind and sea obey?"
On the far shore He frees a man tormented by many demons, who are sent into a herd of swine. The man asks to follow Him and is sent to proclaim what the Lord has done.
A woman is healed by touching His cloak, and He takes the dead daughter of Jairus by the hand: "Talitha koum", "Little girl, I say to you, arise!"
With five loaves and two fish He feeds the multitude, looking up to heaven, blessing and breaking the bread, and twelve baskets of fragments are left over.
In the fourth watch of the night He comes to the disciples walking on the sea. Peter walks toward Him, begins to sink, and cries, "Lord, save me!"
In the synagogue at Capernaum He teaches, "I am the bread of life ... whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life." Peter answers, "Master, to whom shall we go?"
A Gentile mother begs Him to heal her daughter: "Even the dogs eat the scraps that fall from the table of their masters." "O woman, great is your faith!"
He opens the ears of a deaf man, "Ephphatha, be opened", and with seven loaves feeds four thousand who had stayed with Him three days.
Pharisees and Sadducees ask for a sign from heaven. He tells them no sign will be given but the sign of Jonah.
He leads a blind man out of the village by the hand and lays His hands on him twice, until he sees everything distinctly.

"Who do you say that I am?" Peter answers, "You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God." "You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church ... I will give you the keys to the kingdom of heaven."
Before Peter, James and John His face shines like the sun, Moses and Elijah speak with Him, and the Father says, "This is my beloved Son ... listen to him."
He reproaches the towns where most of His mighty deeds had been done, Chorazin, Bethsaida and Capernaum, for they did not repent.
Peter finds the Temple tax in the mouth of a fish. Then Jesus sets a child in their midst: "Unless you turn and become like children, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven."

He teaches in the Temple courts, "Let anyone who thirsts come to me and drink", forgives the woman caught in adultery, "Go, and from now on do not sin any more", and proclaims, "I am the light of the world."
He smears clay on the eyes of a man blind from birth and sends him to wash in the Pool of Siloam. He comes back able to see, and worships Him: "I do believe, Lord."
Martha welcomes Him while Mary sits at His feet listening. "Mary has chosen the better part and it will not be taken from her."
events.u: Luke says only "a village"; John names Bethany as the home of Martha and Mary (John 11:1).

events.s: When a disciple asks Him to teach them to pray, He gives them the Our Father.
events.u: Luke does not name the place; tradition remembers it at the Eleona cave on the Mount of Olives. Matthew gives the prayer in the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 6:9-13).

events.s: Walking in the portico of Solomon in winter, He says, "My sheep hear my voice ... The Father and I are one."
He returns to where John first baptized. He teaches that what God has joined together no one must separate, and blesses the children: "Let the children come to me."
"I am the resurrection and the life." Jesus weeps at the tomb of His friend, then cries out, "Lazarus, come out!", and the dead man walks out, still bound.
As the council plots His death, He withdraws with His disciples to a town near the desert called Ephraim.
Blind Bartimaeus cries, "Jesus, son of David, have pity on me!" and receives his sight. Zacchaeus climbs a sycamore to see Him: "Today salvation has come to this house."
Six days before Passover, Mary anoints His feet with costly nard, and the house is filled with its fragrance. He receives it as an anointing for His burial.
He rides into Jerusalem on a colt as the crowds spread their cloaks and branches: "Hosanna to the Son of David; blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord."
As He comes in sight of the city He weeps over it: "If this day you only knew what makes for peace."
He overturns the tables, "My house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples", and praises the poor widow who gives her last two coins.
Seated on the Mount of Olives facing the Temple, He tells of its destruction and of His coming in glory: "Whatever you did for one of these least brothers of mine, you did for me."

He washes His disciples' feet, and taking bread and wine says, "This is my body ... This cup is the new covenant in my blood ... Do this in memory of me", giving the Church the Holy Eucharist and the priesthood.
He prays in anguish, His sweat like drops of blood: "Father, not my will but yours be done." Judas comes with a crowd and betrays Him with a kiss.
Bound, He is led before Annas and the high priest Caiaphas and condemned for blasphemy. In the courtyard Peter denies Him three times, the cock crows, and Peter weeps bitterly.
Pilate finds no guilt in Him and sends Him to Herod, who mocks Him and sends Him back. The crowd cries out for Barabbas, and Pilate gives in to their demand.
"Then Pilate took Jesus and had him scourged." "By his wounds we were healed" (Isaiah 53:5).
The soldiers weave a crown of thorns, clothe Him in purple and mock Him: "Hail, King of the Jews!" Pilate brings Him out: "Behold, the man!" and hands Him over to be crucified.

Carrying the cross Himself, He goes out toward Golgotha. Simon of Cyrene is made to help Him, and He tells the weeping women, "Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me; weep instead for yourselves and for your children."

He is crucified between two thieves. "Father, forgive them, they know not what they do." "Today you will be with me in Paradise." "Woman, behold, your son ... Behold, your mother." "It is finished." He bows His head and hands over the spirit.
Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus wrap His body in linen with spices and lay Him in a new tomb hewn in the rock, in a garden near the place of the cross.
On the first day of the week the tomb is empty. The risen Lord calls Mary Magdalene by name and sends her to the apostles: "I have seen the Lord."
He walks unrecognized with two disciples, opening the Scriptures to them, and is known to them in the breaking of the bread. "Were not our hearts burning within us?"
He stands among the apostles behind locked doors, breathes on them, "Receive the holy Spirit. Whose sins you forgive are forgiven them", and a week later Thomas confesses, "My Lord and my God!"
At dawn by the lake He fills the apostles' nets and cooks them breakfast. Three times He asks Peter, "Do you love me?" and three times entrusts him: "Feed my sheep."

On the mountain in Galilee He sends the Eleven: "Go, therefore, and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the holy Spirit ... I am with you always."
events.u: Matthew does not name the mountain. Pilgrims often recall it on the Mount of Beatitudes; others think of Tabor or Mount Arbel.

events.s: Forty days after Easter He blesses the apostles, promises them the Holy Spirit, and is taken up to heaven before their eyes, while they return to Jerusalem with great joy.
